name: Walk Down and Static Stretch Sequence
summary: Two slow laps and a fixed order of held stretches for the calves, hamstrings, hips and forearms to finish a session.
setup: Players walk two laps of the court perimeter, then stand in a loose circle beside the court with an arm's length of space each. No equipment; one player leads the sequence and counts the holds out loud.
instructions: Walk two laps of the court, arms swinging, breathing through the nose.
Calf stretch against the fence, thirty seconds each leg.
Hamstring stretch with the heel on the ground and toes up, thirty seconds each leg.
Hip flexor lunge stretch, thirty seconds each side, then a forearm stretch with the palm flat against the fence.
Finish with a thirty-second forward fold and three slow breaths.
coaching_points: Stretch to a gentle pull, never to pain; the muscles are warm and will give.
Breathe out as you settle into each stretch.
Hold still: bouncing tightens the muscle rather than lengthening it.
Keep the back straight in the hamstring stretch; hinge from the hips.
progressions: Hold each stretch for forty-five seconds.
Add a thoracic rotation stretch on the ground.
Add a second round of the calf and hamstring stretches.
regressions: Hold each stretch for twenty seconds.
Walk one lap instead of two.
Do the stretches seated against the fence.

name: Partner Stretch: Hamstrings and Hips
summary: Paired stretches for the hamstrings, groin and hips where one partner supports gently and counts while the other lets go.
setup: Pairs beside the court on a clean patch of ground, or a mat if there is one. One partner stretches while the other supports gently and counts; then they swap. No equipment.
instructions: Lying hamstring stretch: one partner lies on their back and lifts a straight leg; the other supports the heel and holds it at a gentle pull for thirty seconds, then the other leg.
Seated groin stretch: soles of the feet together, the partner presses the knees down lightly for thirty seconds.
Hip rotation: lying on the back, one knee across the body; the partner holds the shoulder down for thirty seconds each side.
Swap roles and repeat.
Finish with both partners standing and shaking out the legs for thirty seconds.
coaching_points: The supporting partner listens: the stretcher says 'there' and the pressure stops.
Breathe out as the leg goes up; the hamstring lets go on the out-breath.
Keep the other leg flat on the ground in the hamstring stretch.
Never push a stretch for a partner; hold, do not press.
progressions: Hold each stretch for forty-five seconds.
Add a contract-relax: push against the partner for five seconds, then relax deeper.
Add a lying quad stretch on the side.
regressions: Hold each stretch for twenty seconds.
Do the stretches alone against the fence instead of with a partner.

name: Breathing and Slow Jog Cool-Down
summary: A slow jog that fades into a walk with counted breathing, bringing the heart rate down before stretching or leaving.
setup: Players jog slowly around the outside of the court in single file, an arm's length apart. No equipment.
instructions: Jog slowly for two minutes around the court, gradually slowing to a walk.
Walk one lap breathing in for four steps and out for six.
Stand still, hands on the head, and take five slow breaths.
Shake out the arms and legs for thirty seconds.
Finish with each player saying one thing they did well in the session.
coaching_points: Jog slower than feels natural; the heart rate should drop, not hold.
Breathe out longer than in; the long out-breath is what slows everything down.
Hands on the head opens the chest for the last breaths.
Keep talking to a minimum until the breathing is settled.
progressions: Jog for three minutes before slowing.
Add a lap of walking lunges before the breathing.
Breathe in for four steps and out for eight.
regressions: One minute of jogging instead of two.
Skip the breathing count and simply walk a lap.

name: Band Recovery Circuit: Shoulders and Forearms
summary: A light resistance band circuit that flushes the shoulders and forearms after a serving-heavy session.
setup: Each player with a light resistance band, standing beside the court with an arm's length of space. The band is held in both hands for the pull-aparts and looped under the front foot for the rows and wrist curls.
instructions: Slow band pull-aparts, ten times, three seconds each way.
Band rows with the band under the front foot, ten times, squeezing the shoulder blades.
Wrist curls with the band under the foot, ten each way.
Forearm stretch with the palm against the fence, thirty seconds each arm.
Finish with slow arm circles, five each way, no band.
coaching_points: Slow and controlled; this is blood flow, not strength work.
Shoulder blades down and together on every row.
Wrist curls: only the wrist moves, the forearm stays on the thigh.
progressions: Hold the forearm stretch for forty-five seconds.
Add an overhead band stretch, arms straight, ten seconds each side.
regressions: Skip the rows and do the pull-aparts twice.
Do the stretches only, with no band.
